### 2026-10-10 – Sat Oct 10:  6:02 PM to 10:30 PM

**4.3h**

Sat Oct 10:  6:02 PM to 10:30 PM

Solved schematic design problems and designed the actual PCB!

During these four hours of hard work, I was filled with so much frustration, and at one point I was about to give up... but I fortuently I didn't.

I started off the first hour trying to solve my schematic design problem. When I ran EMR(Electrical Rules Checker), I still had 3 errors left!! This really made me frustrated, since I didn't know what the errors meant. However, after asking how to fix my error in # Half Life help chat, the person immediately helped me and told me that the error was not a big deal. Thank you so much, #Half Life Help!

Here is a picture of me getting the error and me asking for help from it:

Error:
![error1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/OV6IDpCKgzeGxU5I6u0lX5O426KLPYWz/dbabea44e612de0a830793e0a2a242b2a4037783b75ad2a3e065c52c4f1477bf.png)

Asking for help:

![Erroric](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/OV6IDpCKgzeGxU5I6u0lX5O426KLPYWz/249869f279a3ec6fc39849f6761a888a6eda7982c286291f2238c8711371a870.png)

This lasted me around 1.5 hours. After solving the error, I moved on to the next step of the guide: adding footnotes.

Adding the footnotes was also really frustrating, since this is my first time using KiCAD. I have never ever done PCB before this, so I made SO MANY mistakes(but at least I learned from them!) I realized why three of my footnotes weren't coming up was because I didn't import them into the library. So after importing the files from the Starbie Guide into the library, I was able to search and find them. Then I applied them and almost got ready for PCB design. (KEYWORD: Almost)

I realised just before I was about to make the PCB design that I wanted to add something different. Make my project more unique with different code. Then I looked across my room, trying to figure out what to add. Suddenly, an idea popped into my head: an LED! What if I add an LED to blink so my PCB design would look sick?

I added the LED, wired it to another resistor, and added its own separate footprints by asking Google and getting help from it(since I didn't know footprints for the LED)

Here is an image of my design with the LED included:

![HackClubImages2](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/OV6IDpCKgzeGxU5I6u0lX5O426KLPYWz/76f8e3360906423364e44c8f42c5848b726ca8013e75fdfeac20989cce5f99ad.png)

I was successfully able to add the LED(this took me an hour )

Next, for another  two hours,  I worked on the PCB model itself. I learned a few commands through the help of the Starbie guide and Google. I also watched a great YouTube tutorial on PCB designing(I really loved it!)

I encontured a few problems while PCB desinging:

    1. My microcontroller was always positioned inside the PCB design, and towards the end I realized it should be outside a little, so I can connect a USB port
   2. I kept changing my PCB desing, since I had no design beforehand(bad planning...), and I didn't want to copy the starbie one
   3. Also with the LED, I started to stress out about where to position it.
   4. Also I didn't know most of the commands used to addlines, fillets, and rectangles. I learned through expiermenting, and I was so glad I found the fillet tool(ive used it before in Rhino once)

### 2026-10-11 – October 11:  8:03 AM to 1:40 PM

**5h**

October 11:  8:03 AM to 1:40 PM

During this time, I started routing my PCB connections for each wire. This took me soooo long. I went through so much frustration, and I was so close to giving up. One problem I kept facing was the connections. I needed to make sure on my layer that whenever I connected the route wires (the red ones), they did not cross each other....

I went through multiple problems of the wires overlapping, especially the Gnd, and 3.3v wires. To solve this, I decided to add a fillet.

Solution to my error(the blue part is fillet):
![lol23232](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/OV6IDpCKgzeGxU5I6u0lX5O426KLPYWz/6216ace99f0605a3918428f328f824e5db617d4f78b5bf651f3b985b9c50d954.png)

Basically, I put a ayer of copper for the GND connections, so there was no need to connect the Gnd pins, they were automatically connected!!

After running the DRC, I found 10 errors and 25 warnings!

To solve this problem, I asked for help in  #Half Life Help!

Error:

![Error Help](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/OV6IDpCKgzeGxU5I6u0lX5O426KLPYWz/d7cbfd30c28e5b6676fa5516c1c0821d63964e33b36a0343a7fbbd75c734d729.png)

Help from Hack Club:
![HackClubhelpImages1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/OV6IDpCKgzeGxU5I6u0lX5O426KLPYWz/cd3324c222905962ccbb9861dad9bb45e9dfd267655b48a83c691d6806aed6ac.png)

Anyways, all of that took 2.5 hours, and it was pretty stressful.

After solving the warnings- which were basically unconnected wires and problems with the pin connections- I got ready to upload my New York City design. I uploaded it while routign the wires, but changed some things about it, like the design afterward and placement.

Afterwards, I viewed my model from the 3D editor, and found a few mistakes. I was easily able to fix them with the help of Google:

Editor:

![3DEditor](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/OV6IDpCKgzeGxU5I6u0lX5O426KLPYWz/2278197e8df3712ad7bd11e72722230e138f776a81f76477316a80f063987244.png)

For the first half of the project, I was able to follow the Starbie guide, but after the schematic guide, I started my own things, and well, ended up here with an LED added(since I don't know a lot).

I started coding in Arduino IDE, and im not really good at coding. So I asked for some help from chatgpt, like helping me understand which Libaries I needed to install, and which commands would be important for my code.

Basically, my code works like this: When the left button is pressed, print Hello! on the LCD display and Turn LED on. If the right button is pressed, display the humidity in the air.

This is some aprt of my code, and heres what it does:

1. calls the DHTM1 model to check the humity around the air

2. If left button pressed switch the dispaly using ture or false(bool data type)
